pathQualification.scope: Non-timed private-pointer path qualification only; not a public API contract

scope: Single-host installed public CommonJS package diagnostic with all semantic assertions. Final matched comparison uses 5000 paragraphs / 12 cycles / checkpoints every 3 cycles in reversed process orders. Smaller-document observations have one order only. No Tiptap/GitLab comparison, universal latency, physical-device, production-adoption or full parity claim.
change: Run the existing complete source/factory normalization first. Certify every retained node and text binding at its full previous path against an equivalent expected native result and unchanged index ownership. Reuse only proven unchanged indexes and replace the single changed binding through new map snapshots. Missing/ambiguous/moved bindings, structural changes and reentrant publication retain full reconstruction. No shared map or held coordinate snapshot is mutated in place.
tradeoffs: Final typing medians improve about 8-9 percent in both orders; p95 improves in both, marginally in the reverse pair. Split/wrap medians are 9-28 ms slower in these same runs. In the exploratory 100-paragraph profile the candidate is about 2.1 ms slower per eleven-character burst; the 1000-paragraph median is about 11 ms lower. The change is retained for the repeated large-document typing benefit, not as an across-the-board performance win. Full-document normalization still visits all nodes and remains open work.

supersededInlinePrototype.note: Archival source diff against sourceBase only. Inline-six-cycle results were weak/mixed; the longer inline run improved typing but had slower structural medians. The final isolated helper keeps the ordinary per-node normalization body unchanged. This inline patch is not the retained runtime.

visualReview.observation: Both peers show Paragraph 0500 left in the middle of the 1000-paragraph document; surrounding paragraph order and bold styling remain intact.
Both peers show the matching edited text Aha and BetaZ; the image and caption region remain visible.
The backward text selection is visible in the native editor with peer presence and the retained image.
Both peers show New Planning draft after JSON reopening, with the image retained. Platform font rendering differs; no cross-platform pixel identity is claimed.

corrections: The first new Unicode fixture deleted half a surrogate pair and was correctly rejected by wire validation. Its interval was corrected to delete the complete sequence, with that policy unchanged. The initial non-timed inline path probe omitted a required local user identity and stopped before editor creation; the corrected probe and the final isolated probe succeed. These are not suppressed runtime test failures.
reproduction: Build/pack each source, install its tarball and yjs@13.6.32 in a separate consumer, then run node --expose-gc scripts/diagnose-yjs-endurance.mjs --package-root <consumer>/node_modules/fountainjs-editor --tarball <tarball> --sizes 5000 --cycles 12 --checkpoint-every 3 --output <fresh-report.json>, baseline/candidate then candidate/baseline, serially.
limits: No new dependency, public API, wire format, package-size allowance, capacity/performance/retention limit or weakened test expectation. All acceptance remains subject to full release/hosted CI and the broader collaboration programme.
